question: A network architect designs an infrastructure that enables multiple autonomous workstations, servers, and network printers to exchange data and share hardware resources over transmission media using standardized communication protocols. What fundamental concept does this interconnected system represent?

An enterprise connects its corporate headquarters in New York with regional branch offices in London, Tokyo, and Sydney over leased telecommunications circuits. Which network classification best describes this geographically dispersed infrastructure?
A network engineer configures a full-duplex gigabit Ethernet connection between two core datacenter switches. What is the operational characteristic of this transmission mode?
options: Data can be transmitted and received simultaneously in both directions without collisions
Data can travel in both directions, but only in one direction at a time
Data can only travel in a single fixed direction from sender to receiver
Data packets are broadcast to all connected devices simultaneously
answer: Data can be transmitted and received simultaneously in both directions without collisions

question: In an office local area network, all desktop computers are connected via individual patch cables directly into a central rack-mounted switch. Which network topology is being utilized?

A mission-critical financial exchange requires a network topology where every server is connected to every other server via dedicated links, ensuring zero single points of failure and maximum fault tolerance. Which topology must be deployed?
Why does modern Internet communication rely predominantly on packet switching rather than traditional circuit switching?
options: Packet switching dynamically routes discrete data packets over shared paths, maximizing bandwidth efficiency
Packet switching reserves a dedicated physical wire exclusively for each ongoing communication session
Packet switching eliminates the need for routers, IP addresses, and transport protocols
Packet switching transmits analog audio frequencies rather than digitized binary bits
answer: Packet switching dynamically routes discrete data packets over shared paths, maximizing bandwidth efficiency

question: According to the ISO/IEC 7498-1 standard, into how many conceptual layers is the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model structured?
At which layer of the OSI model do network engineers deal with physical transmission media, signal encoding, pinouts, voltage levels, and raw bit streams?

While analyzing an Ethernet capture in Wireshark, a technician inspects a Layer 2 unit containing source and destination MAC addresses, encapsulated payload, and a Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC/FCS). What is this Layer 2 Protocol Data Unit (PDU) called?

When a packet traverses intermediate networks across the Internet, at which layer of the OSI model does a router inspect logical destination IP addresses and consult routing tables to determine the best path?
Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end communication, segmentation, reassembly, flow control, and port-based multiplexing?
Which layer of the OSI reference model handles data formatting, character code conversion (such as ASCII or Unicode), data compression, and encryption/decryption?
The standard TCP/IP architecture model used by the Internet consolidates networking functions into how many architectural layers?
options: 4 layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, Application
7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
5 layers: Physical, Internet, Transport, Session, Application
answer: 4 layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, Application

question: As application data moves down the TCP/IP protocol stack during encapsulation, what is the correct sequence of Protocol Data Units (PDUs) generated?

An application requires guaranteed, in-order packet delivery with error recovery, whereas a real-time multiplayer game requires low-overhead, fast packet transmission without delivery acknowledgments. Which transport protocols fulfill these respective needs?
options: TCP for reliable delivery, and UDP for low-overhead speed
UDP for reliable delivery, and TCP for low-overhead speed
answer: TCP for reliable delivery, and UDP for low-overhead speed

question: Why does replacing an old Ethernet hub with a modern Layer-2 switch dramatically improve local network performance?
options: A switch inspects MAC addresses to forward frames only to the designated recipient port, creating separate collision domains for each port
A switch broadcasts all incoming electrical signals to every connected port simultaneously
A switch eliminates the need for physical Ethernet cables by converting packets to radio waves
A switch operates exclusively at the Physical layer to boost analog voltage levels
answer: A switch inspects MAC addresses to forward frames only to the designated recipient port, creating separate collision domains for each port

question: A network technician needs to connect two separate IP subnets (192.168.1.0/24 and 10.0.0.0/24) so that computers in both subnets can communicate. Which networking device must be deployed?
Which hardware device operates at the Physical layer (Layer 1) to amplify or regenerate electrical/optical signals, overcoming signal attenuation over long cable distances?
What is the primary role of a network firewall positioned at an enterprise boundary?
options: To monitor, inspect, and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predefined security rules
To convert digital computer signals into analog telephone frequencies
To assign physical MAC addresses to connected workstations
To distribute electrical alternating current power to connected network switches
answer: To monitor, inspect, and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predefined security rules

question: How many total bits compose a standard IPv4 address, and how is it conventionally represented for human readability?
options: 32 bits, expressed as four decimal octets separated by dots
64 bits, expressed as eight decimal octets separated by dashes
128 bits, expressed as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
48 bits, expressed as twelve hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens
answer: 32 bits, expressed as four decimal octets separated by dots

question: To address IPv4 address exhaustion, IPv6 was introduced with vastly expanded address space. What is the total bit length of an IPv6 address?
Every Network Interface Card (NIC) is manufactured with a globally unique physical hardware address. What is the standard length of this MAC address?
When calculating the number of usable host IP addresses in a subnet using the formula 2^h - 2 (where h is the number of host bits), why is 2 subtracted?
options: The first address represents the Network ID and the last address represents the Directed Broadcast Address
One address is reserved for the default gateway and one for the primary DNS server
One address is reserved for the DHCP server and one for the hardware firewall
One address is reserved for the loopback interface and one for the switch management port
answer: The first address represents the Network ID and the last address represents the Directed Broadcast Address

question: A network engineer allocates the CIDR block 192.168.10.0/26 to a department. What is the dotted-decimal subnet mask and the maximum number of usable host IP addresses on this subnet?
options: Subnet mask 255.255.255.192 with 62 usable host addresses
Subnet mask 255.255.255.128 with 126 usable host addresses
Subnet mask 255.255.255.224 with 30 usable host addresses
Subnet mask 255.255.255.0 with 254 usable host addresses
answer: Subnet mask 255.255.255.192 with 62 usable host addresses

question: Host A needs to send an IP packet to Host B on the same local subnet. Host A knows Host B IP address (192.168.1.50) but does not have Host B MAC address in its local cache. Which protocol broadcasts a request to resolve the IP address into a MAC address?
When a new client device connects to an enterprise Wi-Fi network, which protocol automatically assigns it an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS servers using the 4-step DORA process?
When a user types www.example.com into a web browser, which protocol resolves this human-friendly hostname into a numerical IP address, typically utilizing UDP or TCP port 53?
Why does modern web browsing strongly favor HTTPS over standard HTTP?
options: HTTPS encrypts communications using TLS/SSL over port 443 to safeguard confidentiality and data integrity
HTTPS eliminates packet headers to double transmission speed
HTTPS allows web pages to be viewed without an active Internet connection
HTTPS disables cookies and cache storage entirely on web browsers
answer: HTTPS encrypts communications using TLS/SSL over port 443 to safeguard confidentiality and data integrity

question: A systems administrator needs to remotely manage a Linux server securely from across the Internet. Which protocol provides encrypted command-line terminal communication over TCP port 22, replacing unencrypted Telnet?

A network engineer runs the command ping 8.8.8.8 from a terminal to test network connectivity and measure round-trip latency. Which underlying protocol sends the Echo Request and listens for the Echo Reply?
